nodes.procedure: Then the CeO2 film was immersed in cobalt(II) nitrate solution for 60 min to obtain a layer of fine (about 0.25 nm) and uniform cobaltous oxide (CoO) nanosheets on the surface of CeO2, forming a large number of interfaces between CoO and CeO2.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM shows fine and uniform CoO nanosheets growing on the surface of CeO2 layer for CoO/CeO2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The SEM image of CoO/CeO2 is shown in Figure 1a, where fine and uniform CoO nanosheets grow on the surface of CeO2 layer.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cross-sectional TEM shows CoO nanosheets layer (green lines region) ~0.25 nm thick on CeO2 substrate with clear CoO/CeO2 interfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 1b is the cross-sectional transmission electron microscopy (TEM) image of the CoO/CeO2 sample, clearly showing the cross-sectional distribution, in which the region within the green lines is the surface CoO nanosheets layer.

properties.features: Purple staining, nanostructured morphology with dark aggregates and lighter matrix

properties.description: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy image showing nanostructured material with fibrous or porous morphology

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM elemental mapping shows uniform Ce and O distribution in CeO2 substrate and uniform Co and O distribution in upper CoO nanosheet layer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-angle annular dark field-scanning TEM (HAADF-STEM) image and the corresponding elemental mapping images of CoO/CeO2 are shown in Figure 1d.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM confirms CoO (111) lattice spacing of 2.4 Å and CeO2 (111) lattice spacing of 3.1 Å at CoO/CeO2 interface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The interplanar spacing of CoO is determined to be 2.4 Å (site 1, Figure S5a), which is identical with the lattice planes of CoO (1 1 1)... The interplanar spacing of CeO2 is determined to be 3.1 Å (site 2, Figure S5b), which is identical with the lattice planes of CeO2 (1 1 1).

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman shows CeO2 peak at ~460 cm⁻¹ (fluorite structure, good crystallinity) and weak Co-O peak at ~530 cm⁻¹ due to ultrathin CoO nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of CoO/CeO2 in Figure 1f shows two peaks at ~460 cm⁻¹ and ~530 cm⁻¹, which originated from the fluorite-type structure of CeO2 and the Co-O in CoO, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p3/2 binding energy shifts from 781 eV (CoO) to 780.88 eV (CoO/CeO2) indicating electronic interaction; Ce 3d shows 26% Ce3+ concentration.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Co 2p XPS spectra of the CoO/CeO2 and CoO samples are shown in Figure 1g, where the 2p3/2 of CoO/CeO2 and CoO locate at 780.88 and 781 eV, respectively, corresponding to Co-O of CoO... According to their relative areas, the concentration of Ce3+ was calculated to be 26%.

nodes.characterization_summary: LSV polarization curves (10 mV/s, iR compensated) show CoO/CeO2 overpotential of 291 mV at 10 mA/cm² vs CoO (327 mV) and RuO2 (332 mV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2a shows the LSV polarization curves of CoO/CeO2, CoO, and RuO2 (reference sample) with iR compensation. The CoO/CeO2 catalyst displays the smallest overpotential of 291 mV to reach the current density of 10 mA/cm², while CoO and RuO2 need larger overpotentials of 327 mV and 332 mV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS Nyquist plots (0.1-10^5 Hz) show CoO/CeO2 has smallest Rct semicircle radius and Rs, indicating fastest charge transfer kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Nyquist plot in Figure 2b (measure frequency from 10^-1 to 10^5 Hz) shows that the semicircle radius of CoO/CeO2 electrode is much smaller than that of CoO and RuO2, indicating the smallest charge transfer resistance (Rct).

nodes.characterization_summary: Tafel slope of CoO/CeO2 is 84 mV/dec, lower than CoO and RuO2, indicating superior OER kinetics.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Tafel slope of CoO/CeO2 in Figure 2c is determined as 84 mV/dec, lower than that of CoO and RuO2, indicating its better inherent OER activity and superior OER kinetics.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV at various scan rates determines Cdl proportional to ECSA; CoO/CeO2 shows lower ECSA but higher intrinsic activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemically active surface areas (ECSAs) of these catalysts were proportional to the double-layer capacitances (Cdl), which were calculated from cyclic voltammograms (CV) measurements under different scan rates.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-OES shows no detectable Co or Ce ions in electrolyte after 100h stability test, confirming ultrahigh stability of CoO/CeO2.
